source.title: Applying sparse autoencoders to unlearn knowledge in language models
source.authors: Eoin Farrell; Yeu-Tong Lau; Arthur Conmy

record.tranche_reason: It measures the loss added when model activations are replaced by SAE reconstructions, bearing on one part of V3, but does not compare with random errors matched in size.
record.gate_note: Appendix B reports reconstruction-induced loss for two models. The paper does not test linear predictability, error scaling or token overlap, the two proposed kinds of dark matter, or whether SAE-based analyses lose behavior. Its feature-clamping and unlearning results concern different interventions and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE-based unlearning study that uses SAEs as a tool and reports its own method's performance. The one dark-matter-adjacent number is a check that base-model SAEs transfer to the chat model. That check reports reconstruction loss added, about 0.86 for gemma-2-2b and 0.89 for gemma-2-2b-it (units not stated, probably nats). It has no random-error comparison, so it cannot show whether the errors are pathological (V3). The interventions keep the SAE error term (Fig. 1), but the paper never tests what happens without it (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Individual SAE features, clamped to negative values, can unlearn a subset of WMDP-bio questions with small side effects; zero-ablating them is ineffective. Using 10-20 features unlearns much of WMDP-bio but with similar or larger MMLU side effects than RMU. SAE quality or intervention methods need major improvement to rival fine-tuning. Separately, Appendix B's reconstruction-loss figures are taken to show base-to-chat SAE transfer.
record.recipe_differences: Measures loss from replacing activations with SAE reconstructions; does not use the matched random-error comparison specified in V3 or investigate the other dark-matter measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Splicing Gemma Scope SAE reconstructions into gemma-2-2b adds 0.8631 loss over 409K OpenWebText tokens; into gemma-2-2b-it it adds 0.8860. Units are not stated, probably nats. The authors read this as evidence that the SAE transfers from base to chat model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on a base model reconstruct the chat model's activations with similar loss added (cross-model SAE transfer).

record.problems: For the reconstruction-loss result, no random-error comparison or uncertainty estimate is reported.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error is not measured.
Error scaling across SAE sizes and per-token overlap are not measured.
There is no comparison against random errors of matched norm.
There is no split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
The error term is preserved in all interventions, but there is no ablation of it.
There is no comparison across SAE training methods or architectures with respect to error.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification is too generous. A bare reconstruction loss used to validate a tool does not test V3's comparative claim. The rows are kept as cannot_determine, and no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure whether SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation.
The study does not measure per-token error norms across SAE sizes, whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts, or whether error persists with scale.
It measures loss added by SAE reconstruction, but does not compare that effect with random errors of the same size.
The study does not separate predictable and nonlinear error or test their relation to learned features and further dictionary learning.
The study does not test whether SAE-feature-based circuits or steering lose behavior when the error term is omitted.
The study does not test whether dark matter is caused by SAE training choices or shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.
